body:
FOUND BY T113's round-8 review. `parseArgs` (src/cli/args.ts:24-27) sends any `--name=value` to `parsed.flags`, never to `parsed.booleans`. A declared boolean is read from `booleans`, so writing it with a value passes the allowlist and is then invisible.

The harmless case: `loam user unlock --all=1` refuses with 'wants a name' — the wrong reason, but it refuses.

THE FOOTGUN: `loam user create myk --operator=true` succeeds and creates a PLAIN ACTOR. The operator asked for the operator role, the command reported success, and the role is not there. That is H7's shape at the CLI — an operation reporting a success it did not achieve — and it is silent, so nobody learns until a door refuses them later.

The fix is in the parser, once, for every boolean: `parseArgs` must REFUSE `--name=value` when `name` is a declared boolean, with a message naming the flag and that it takes no value. A boolean written with a value is always a mistake, never an intent worth guessing.

Rails: (a) every declared boolean, refused with a value, for at least two commands; (b) `loam user create <name> --operator=true` exits non-zero and appends NOTHING (delta count before and after) — the two-sided form, because the danger here is a partial success; (c) the bare boolean still works, so the fix did not break the ordinary path.

Repair tier: this restores what the flag already promises. Self-mergeable on a clean bar.
title: A declared boolean flag written as --flag=value is silently ignored — `loam user create myk --operator=true` makes a plain actor
